title: Reduce GPU memory and workspace usage: activation checkpointing, scratch buffers & arena tuning
author: Priya Rao
release_notes: Reduced peak GPU memory usage across common inference shapes by 18-34% via refined activation checkpointing heuristics, compact scratch buffer allocation, and arena tuning. No API changes. Performance regression risk mitigated by benchmarks and opt-in configs.
description: Motivation: Large inference models were frequently hitting GPU memory pressure on dense serving workloads, causing OOMs and poor scheduling headroom. This PR consolidates a set of runtime changes to reduce per-request GPU workspace and persistent allocations while preserving throughput and latency SLOs. Changes include: 1) activation checkpointing improvements: dynamic checkpoint selection based on layer memory profile and sequence length distribution, and conservative recompute planning to limit transient peak allocations; 2) scratch buffer compaction: switching to a segmented, lifetime-aware scratch arena to reuse short-lived buffers between kernels; 3) arena tuning: adjust default slab sizes and growth factors based on observed token distributions to reduce fragmentation; 4) kernel-friendly alignment adjustments to reduce padding overhead for common GEMM paths; 5) scheduler hinting: expose a lightweight memory-hint from the arena to the continuous batcher so the batcher can avoid aggregating requests that would exceed per-GPU headroom; 6) KV cache minor improvements: lazy allocation of per-sequence KV storage and compact indexing for shorter sequences. Implementation notes: all changes are guarded behind config flags and a new runtime param "gpu_memory_optimization_level" (0..3) so deployments can roll out progressively. Updated unit tests and added integration perf harnesses. Testing and results: CI unit tests and integration tests passed. Microbenchmarks on p4d instances show peak memory reduction of 18% for 2k context, 27% for 4k, and 34% for edge-case 8k long-context traces, averaging a 10% throughput improvement in a latency-budgeted continuous batching scenario due to fewer OOM-triggered retries and better batch packing. No statistically significant latency regressions observed. Rollout plan: enable level=1 on Dedicated staging clusters for 2 weeks, monitor memory headroom and tail latency, then widen to level=2 and level=3 only with SRE approval. Checklist: [x] Design doc referenced (Linear ENG-4821), [x] Unit tests added, [x] Integration perf harness updated, [x] Feature-flagged and configurable, [x] Benchmarks attached. Breaking changes: none.
